column1: # Stage 1 of finding each solver's best single configuration: the knobs never
# measured at all.
# Everything published so far moved one factor at a time from a fixed baseline,
# and stopped as soon as something worked. That leaves holes, and the larger
# set of them is STP's: of the nine settings KLEE exposes for it, the tuned
# configuration sets four.
# --stp-bv-abstraction-width is the pointed one. It is STP's own version of the
# abstraction whose Bitwuzla counterpart was measured here, its comment in
# STPSolver.cpp says outright that "GSL is almost entirely double, so this
# suite sits on the losing side of that split; measuring it is the point", and
# it has been sitting at off throughout. 53 is the binary64 significand, 24 the
# binary32 one.
# The two incremental-simplification flags exist because STP's per-level route
# "hands the SAT solver a formula nobody has been over". Both default off and
# neither has been measured against this corpus.
# On Bitwuzla's side the hole is narrower and just as obvious: rewrite level 1
# beat the default 2 by 7.5%, and nobody asked whether 0 beats 1.
# One factor per row. Interactions are stage 2, deliberately -- a second
# one-at-a-time pass cannot see them.
# label <TAB> backend <TAB> LD_LIBRARY_PATH for libstp (or -) <TAB> extra klee args
stp-best
stp-piece
stp-scoped
stp-bvabs53
stp-bvabs24
bwz-rwl1
bwz-rwl0
